catalog_quote: Phonological word shape: sesquisyllabic word structure in which presyllables are unstressed and somewhat reduced in form, consonant clusters on main syllables ... As in many Mon-Khmer languages, Kơho has two syllable types: a presyllable and a main syllable. The prototypical full phonological word (PW) takes a sesquisyllabic (‘syllable and a half’) form (Matisoff 1973:86). Thus, a word in Sre may be defined as consisting of a main syllable, optionally preceded by a presyllable (7). (7) PW = (presyllable) + Main syllable Metrically, such phonological words constitute an iambic construction of the type ( ̆ . --). ... Presyllables tend to weaken or disappear in many environments. ... Long vowels decrease in duration when they are not at the end of a word, particularly if unstressed. ... audit.reasoning: Quote check: every fragment of the deciding quotation is verbatim in the Olsen 2014 text we hold layer at the cited pages (p.14 sec 1.3; pp.30-34 secs 2.3-2.4). Deciding source is a 2014 descriptive-grammar dissertation by a long-term fieldworker with its own acoustic measurements; it is the most recent of the grammars Glottolog lists. I downloaded the other English grammar (Manley 1971 UH dissertation = OLSP 12, 1972) from ScholarSpace; its section 2.4 'Accent' states independently that in presyllable+major-syllable words 'the pre-syllable receives weak accent and the major syllable receives primary accent', plus a pause-group rule (last lexical formative keeps primary accent). sources.quote: 'Here we shall distinguish three accents: primary, medium, and weak. None of these is phonemic. For citation form, in morphemes consisting of a single syllable, there is primary accent on that syllable. For words composed, phonologically, of a minor syllable, or pre-syllable, and a major syllable, the pre-syllable receives weak accent and the major syllable receives primary accent.' Adds a phrase-level rule: in connected discourse lexical formatives reduce to medium accent unless they are the last lexical formative in the pause group, which keeps primary accent; grammatical formatives never ex
